label: Town of New Haven
header:
# Town of New Haven municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 16; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: Town of New Haven (official website), Selectboard page: lists the five-member selectboard as John Roleau (Chair), Marie Jewett, Mike Audy, Bruce Many (Vice Chair), and Shauntell Barnum, printing a two-year term ending 2028 for Barnum

Town of New Haven (official website), Elections page: publishes the official marked ballot for the March 3, 2026 annual town meeting (364 ballots cast), recording John Roleau re-elected with 319 votes and Marie Jewett re-elected with 343 votes; the selectboard page's printed term expiries for Roleau and Jewett are stale and the certified results govern

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): carries a single New Haven row naming Shauntell Barnum; the directory is incomplete for this town and the town's own sources govern. The 2025 annual report seated Chris Bataille on the board in Barnum's place; the transition is not explained in any official source located, and Barnum is recorded as the elected member the current pages present
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): names Pamela Kingman as New Haven's town clerk
Town of New Haven (official website), Town Reports page: the 2025 annual report's officers table and the 2026 warning (Art. 6) carry Kingman as town clerk for a term to 2028
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): names Julie Bessette as New Haven's town treasurer
Town of New Haven (official website), Town Reports page: the 2025 annual report's officers table carries Bessette as town treasurer for a term to 2028

offices.org_name: New Haven Collector of Delinquent Taxes

sources.note: Town of New Haven (official website), Town Reports page: the town's officers table and warning elect a collector of delinquent taxes separately; Julie Bessette holds the office for a term to 2028
Town of New Haven (official website), Town Reports page: the 2025 annual report's officers table lists listers Ted Foster (to 2028), Julie Bessette, and Jay Best, Jr.

Town of New Haven (official website), Elections page: the official March 3, 2026 ballot records Julie Bessette elected to the three-year lister seat with 349 votes (she had been appointed to fill a vacancy) and Jay Best, Jr. elected to the one-year lister seat with 323 votes
Town of New Haven (official website), Town Reports page: the 2025 annual report's officers table lists auditors Ted Foster (to 2028), Mary Pratt (to 2027), and Ellie de Villiers (to 2028)

Town of New Haven (official website), Elections page: the official March 3, 2026 ballot records Pam Marsh elected moderator with 315 votes, to the new three-year term; Marsh is the Addison Probate District's judge of probate and her existing person record is reused

Town of New Haven (official website), Town Reports page: the 2025 annual report's officers table lists five library trustees: Kristen Swartzentruber (to 2028), Darcy Cummings (to 2028), Kim Callahan, Erika Smith, and Sujata Moorti (appointed after Leanne Gund resigned)

Town of New Haven (official website), Elections page: the official March 3, 2026 ballot records Kim Callahan re-elected with 333 votes, Molly Bull elected with 332 votes (Erika Smith's seat), and Sujata Moorti elected to the one-year remainder with 335 votes

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists seven New Haven justices of the peace elected November 5, 2024; two have since resigned (see the election note), leaving five serving

jp_election.name: Town of New Haven Justice of the Peace Election 2024-11-05

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists seven New Haven justices of the peace elected November 5, 2024: Kathleen Barrett, Tim Bouton, Gail Freidin, Al Karnatz, Marie Jewett, Pam Marsh, and Susan Smiley. The town's 2025 annual report records that Gail Freidin (printed there as 'Gail Byers'; the listing's form governs) resigned in November 2025 and Susan Smiley resigned in January 2026, so five of the seven winners currently serve and are the winners recorded here; Freidin and Smiley, as departed winners, are named in this note only (the Enosburgh/Maidstone pattern). The listing publishes no vote totals or party labels and none are recorded

Town of New Haven (official website), Town Reports page: the 2025 annual report's officers table records the resignations of justices of the peace Gail Freidin (November 2025) and Susan Smiley (January 2026)
